steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Successful compositions show DEVELOPMENT, not just repetition — musical ideas are extended, varied, transformed and combined across sections.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Structural planning before composing: decide on form, key relationships, textural changes and dynamic shape — this prevents aimless meandering.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Contrasting sections create musical interest: vary texture (thick/thin), dynamics (loud/soft), harmony (tense/resolved), melody (legato/staccato).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Linking to Areas of Study strengthens your composition: use elements from your chosen AoS as inspiration for style, harmony and structure.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how composition techniques and development are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use composition techniques and development. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use composition techniques and development in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how composition techniques and development are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comp | A practical application showing understanding of how composition techniques and development can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
